subsenses.definition: (transitive) To impart or transmit (information or knowledge) to someone; to make known, to tell.
examples: It is vital that I communicate this information to you.

subsenses.definition: (transitive) To impart or transmit (an intangible quantity, substance); to give a share of.
examples: to communicate motion by means of a crank

subsenses.definition: (transitive) To pass on (a disease) to another person, animal etc.
examples: The disease was mainly communicated via rats and other vermin.

subsenses.definition: (transitive, obsolete) To share (in); to have in common, to partake of.
examples: We shall now consider those functions of intelligence which man communicates with the higher beasts.
